key_insight: The band alignment at 3D/2D perovskite interfaces is highly sensitive to surface termination, cleavage, and chemical composition, causing measurable shifts in work function and band offsets.
engineering_relevance: These interface-dependent electronic shifts must be controlled to design stable 2D/3D perovskite solar cells with reliable passivation and improved device performance.
method: Atomistic modeling of (PEA)2PbI4 on mixed-cation/mixed-halide 3D perovskites
Consistent calculation of work function, electron affinity, and band offsets
evidence_signal: Preliminary simulations show strong work-function dependence on surface chemistry, interface-induced macroscopic potential slopes, and band offsets spanning roughly 0.2–0.7 eV for valence bands and about 0.25 eV for conduction bands.
watch_item: Results are preliminary and appear sensitive to surface termination and polarization effects, so interface-specific conclusions may not generalize across all perovskite compositions or processing conditions.
paper_title: Material chemical composition impacts on the band alignments: preliminary results on the 3D/2D perovskite interfaces
